newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: South Africa's rand clung to its firmer levels in late trade, receiving an extra boost from a sliding U.S. dollar on markets overseas.
Dealers said the softer dollar against the key mark and yen crosses helped the rand to near the 4.4600 level in the absence of local factors.
"The rand is just drifting gently better on the dollar. There is no real trade worth to speak about here," a dealer said.
At 1407 GMT the rand was changing hands at 4.4620/4650 on the dollar from 4.4700/4730 late on Thursday.
The dollar took a fresh lurch lower in early U.S. dealings, cracking support at 1.6980 against the mark and dipping below 121.50 yen, on scaled back expectations of a rise in U.S. interest rates.
Comments from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, although variously interpreted by the market, were seen by many as reducing the chances of a rate tightening later this month.

Greenspan said he expected economic growth to slow later this year, but that the Fed would need to act were that not so. He noted scant evidence of an imminent inflation pick-up but argued labour markets were tight and the economy had little slack.
Local dealers said an early export order was met by small amounts of dollar demand from offshore and domestic players in the afternoon, but overall volumes were light.
"After yesterday's big dollar order worked itself out, nothing much has happened," a dealer said.

On Thursday the rand slipped to a two-month low of 4.4795 bid following an order linked to South African firm Illovo Sugar Ltd's purchase of Lonrho Sugar Corp from U.K-based Lonrho Plc for over 1.6 billion rand.
Dealers predicted a range of 4.4550-4.4800 for the rand for next week.

Against the crosses, the rand was last at 7.2203/7.2296 on sterling from 7.2224/2412 late on Wednesday. On the mark it was trading at 0.3794/3797 from 0.3828/3831 before, and at 27.2350/2946 yen from 28.0570/0871 yen previously.
On the bond market the key R150 long bond was little changed at 14.915 percent in late dealings from 14.920 percent on Thursday.

Dealers said trade during the afternoon was characterised by a squaring of positions, and as local institutions had been very inactive, the market had been closely watching the U.S. Treasury bond which had been volatile.

The U.S. bond was last firmer at 6.88 percent as Treasuries extended their gains in heavy mid-morning trade as players bought on hopes that the Federal Reserve will not move on interest rates at its May 20 meeting.
"Some people are now talking of a rally in the U.S. It seems to be the lead indicator in our market at the moment and if that happens, then rates will be down on Monday," a dealer said.
However, in the absence of such a move, dealers said the market was difficult to call, with economic fundamentals pointing positive but technical market factors leaning to the negative.
Traders said the fact that the rand had recovered from its lows on Thursday had removed pressure from offshore to sell bonds.
The Bond Exchange said that foreigners were net sellers of 25.79 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Thursday after buying 139.93 million rand's worth on Wednesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes amounted to 35.89 billion rand -- a settlement date -- from 9.18 billion rand previously.
On the money market major banks kept their three month deposit rates steady at between 16.40 to 16.45 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at between 15.80 to 15.95 percent.
The Reserve Bank said the daily money market shortage edged up to 8.955 billion rand on Thursday after falling to 8.908 billion rand on Wednesday.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
